author: Matthias Bastian
content_snippet:
In a blog post, complexity theorist and former OpenAI researcher Scott Aaronson lays out what AI's recent math breakthroughs might mean for the rest of us.

Proving the Riemann hypothesis probably wouldn't change anyone's daily life, Aaronson writes. The ideas behind work like that could lead to new applications in science and engineering down the road, but it's anyone's guess which ones.

Aaronson, a professor at the University of Texas at Austin, argues the far bigger deal is that AI can do th
summary_en: Scott Aaronson, professor at UT Austin and former OpenAI researcher, argues the significance of AI math breakthroughs lies in the system's ability to explore mathematical truth, not just the specific proofs. He emphasizes that establishing lower bounds in matrix multiplication and Fourier transforms reveals hard computational limits and signals a potential breakthrough in the P vs NP problem.

author: Matthias Bastian
content_snippet:

summary_en: OpenAI engineer Thibault Sottiaux confirmed that a billing bug during the GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol rollout has been rectified. The fix results in a 40% and 25% faster consumption rate for Astra and Sol quotas respectively, while the company provides extra resets and free Fast Mode access for subscribers as compensation.

inline_images.caption: SAP reportedly weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in fresh restructuring
inline_images.alt: SAP reportedly weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in fresh restructuring

author: Bloomberg
content_snippet: SAP SE is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions to transform its software business for the artificial intelligence era …
summary_en: SAP CEO Christian Klein and CFO Dominik Asam are evaluating a restructuring plan to cut at least 10,000 positions, aiming to accelerate the firm's pivot toward cloud and AI-oriented roles. This initiative deviates from the previous 'Project Mongoose' strategy, which targeted incremental 1-2% annual workforce reductions to address execution lags in the earlier 'Next Level Transformation' program.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: SAP首席执行官Christian Klein与首席财务官Dominik Asam正评估一项新的重组计划，拟裁减至少1万名员工。此举旨在修正此前“Next Level Transformation”执行进度滞后的问题，通过大规模结构性调整将人力资源向AI与云业务倾斜，打破了原定通过“Project Mongoose”进行年均1-2%小规模削减的既定规划。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: SAP CEO Christian Klein and CFO Dominik Asam are evaluating a restructuring plan to cut at least 10,000 positions, aiming to accelerate the firm's pivot toward cloud and AI-oriented roles. This initiative deviates from the previous 'Project Mongoose' strategy, which targeted incremental 1-2% annual workforce reductions to address execution lags in the earlier 'Next Level Transformation' program.

fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】SAP首席执行官Christian Klein、首席财务官Dominik Asam在企业内部组织重组计划：拟裁减至少1万个工作岗位以强化AI与云业务布局
【起因与机理】此前转型计划执行进度不及预期，需通过激进的结构重组实现生产力跃升
【关键数据与实测】企业拟裁减超1万名员工，约为总人数的10%。

fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Christian Klein (CEO) and Dominik Asam (CFO) of SAP (Internal corporate restructuring): Considering cutting at least 10,000 roles to accelerate AI/cloud transition
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Previous transformation execution fell behind; radical structural adjustment needed for productivity

[Key Position & Outlook] Core focus shifted to AI-driven productivity gains in cloud services.

title: Avicena, which links AI chips with microLEDs instead of lasers, raised a $100M+ Series C led by Intervest, with participation from SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD (Cristian Dina/The Next Web)
title_en: Avicena, which links AI chips with microLEDs instead of lasers, raised a $100M+ Series C led by Intervest, with participation from SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD (Cristian Dina/The Next Web)

inline_images.caption: Avicena’s connectorised LightBundle microLED link, shown in September 2026 Credit: Avicena
inline_images.alt: Avicena’s connectorised LightBundle microLED link, shown in September 2026 Credit: Avicena

author: The Next Web
content_snippet:
Avicena, a Sunnyvale startup that links AI chips with tiny LEDs instead of lasers, has raised more than $100M in Series C funding. It also has a new chief executive. Kevin Pope succeeds Marco Chisari and will lead the company as it brings its first product to market next year.

InterVest led the round, Avicena announced on Tuesday. Other investors include Tiger Global, Cerberus Capital Management, SK hynix Ventures, Samsung Catalyst Fund and AMD Ventures. Prosperity7 Ventures, Mitsubishi Chemica
summary_en: Sunnyvale-based Avicena has raised over $100M in Series C funding, led by InterVest with participation from SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD. The company's LightBundle platform utilizes MicroLED arrays instead of traditional lasers to address bandwidth and power bottlenecks in data movement between processors and memory in AI clusters.

title: Texas resumes data centre permitting before Democrats take over
title_en: Texas resumes data centre permitting before Democrats take over
author: Stephanie Findlay
content_snippet: Incoming governor Gina Hinojosa pledged to rein in construction of new projects during her campaign — Hello and welcome to Energy Source, coming to you from Houston.
summary_en: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has resumed environmental permitting for data centers under a directive from outgoing Republican Governor Greg Abbott. The approvals include SpaceX's $24 billion gas-fired power and supercomputing complex near Brownsville, as developers scramble to secure rights before incoming Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa takes office in January with a mandate to curtail industry expansion and tax incentives.
subheadings: Follow the topics in this article

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 德克萨斯州环境质量委员会（TCEQ）在共和党籍现任州长格雷格·阿博特（Greg Abbott）的指令下，正式重启数据中心相关项目的环境许可审批。该批次获批项目包含SpaceX位于布朗斯维尔附近价值240亿美元的天然气发电与超算设施，旨在赶在明年1月民主党籍准州长吉娜·伊诺霍萨（Gina Hinojosa）上任、预计实施开发限制及取消税收优惠政策前完成关键部署。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has resumed environmental permitting for data centers under a directive from outgoing Republican Governor Greg Abbott. The approvals include SpaceX's $24 billion gas-fired power and supercomputing complex near Brownsville, as developers scramble to secure rights before incoming Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa takes office in January with a mandate to curtail industry expansion and tax incentives.

fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】德克萨斯州环境质量委员会（TCEQ）、州长格雷格·阿博特、准州长吉娜·伊诺霍萨、SpaceX在美国德克萨斯州：重启数据中心项目审批，批准包括SpaceX在内的能源设施许可
【起因与机理】利用政权更迭前的窗口期，规避新政府可能实施的开发限制与政策不确定性
【关键数据与实测】SpaceX获批240亿美元天然气电站与超算中心许可。
【各方立场与态度】防范准州长伊诺霍萨上任后可能实施的 moratorium（开发禁令）及税收优惠清理。

[Key Metrics] SpaceX secures permits for a $24B gas power plant and supercomputing facility.
[Key Position & Outlook] Developers aim to beat potential moratoriums and tax cut rollbacks under Governor-elect Hinojosa.

title: FCC clears SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites for orbital AI data centers by 2040

author: Maximilian Schreiner
content_snippet:
SpaceX has won approval from US communications regulators for its Starmind constellation. Up to 1 million satellites would process AI data in orbit.

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites for orbital data centers, according to Reuters. The Starmind constellation of orbital compute modules is intended to meet part of the rapidly growing demand for AI computing power on Earth. The agency also approved radio links that let SpaceX moni
summary_en: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites as part of the 'Starmind' constellation. This initiative aims to establish orbital compute modules for processing AI data to alleviate terrestrial compute demand, with approvals covering radio links for satellite monitoring and control redundancy.

author: Martin Arnold and Nikou Asgari
content_snippet: FCA points to Binance heist and ‘lack of consumer protections’ as reasons for tighter regulation of decentralised finance than in US and EU
summary_en: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), led by Jane Moore (Head of Payments and Digital Assets), plans to mandate authorization for DeFi platforms to close regulatory gaps in anti-money laundering and consumer protection. Regulators emphasize that the recent $6.3 billion Binance hack, where stolen assets flowed through DeFi protocols for laundering, necessitates stricter oversight beyond current market norms.

title: ASML’s CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
title_en: ASML’s CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
author: Reed Albergotti
content_snippet:
Export controls on chips and other technology shouldn’t aim to cut China off completely — a strategy that will only backfire, warns Christophe Fouquet, CEO of ASML, the sole maker of the lithography machines needed to produce the world’s most advanced AI chips.

“You need [export controls] to protect very advanced technology, but you also have to use export control in such a way that you don’t completely frustrate a country and invite that country to basically double down or triple down on devel
summary_en: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet argued that export controls should target only the most advanced technology rather than a total blockade. He warned that over-restricting China forces domestic acceleration in chip development, whereas maintaining a 'generation gap' via older equipment exports keeps Beijing tethered to Western hardware ecosystems.

content_snippet:
Confidential data sent to Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) startup MiniMax (0100.HK) was accessed by unidentified third parties, it has emerged. The finding was disclosed by HD Moore, chief research officer (CRO) of US cybersecurity firm Dragos, who said the access occurred even when users specified they did not want their data stored or retained.

summary_en: Dragos Chief Research Officer HD Moore revealed that AI startup MiniMax improperly stores private web links from user prompts despite opt-out requests. author: The Record
content_snippet:
State-backed hacking groups in China and North Korea are using a powerful AI hacking tool in attacks, according to a new report from Microsoft.

Microsoft explained that state-sponsored and financially motivated hackers are using Artex, an AI-powered platform that can automate multiple phases of cyber intrusions at machine speed.

summary_en: Microsoft reports that state-sponsored hacking groups, including Salt Typhoon, have integrated the AI-powered penetration testing tool ARTEX into their offensive arsenals. title: 2 California companies are buying Nvidia's most advanced chips. Those companies are actually Chinese-owned, a CBS News investigation reveals.
title_en: 2 California companies are buying Nvidia's most advanced chips. Those companies are actually Chinese-owned, a CBS News investigation reveals.
author: Josh Boswell
content_snippet:
Nvidia is selling its most cutting-edge chips to at least two companies that are U.S.-based, but are actually controlled by Chinese-owned firms, raising fresh questions about efforts to keep sensitive technology away from the nation's rivals, a CBS News investigation found.

One of the chip giant's "preferred partners" is a California company owned by a Chinese firm whose chief executive is a graduate of a Chinese military university, records show. Another California company was renamed after it
summary_en: Investigations reveal that several California-based NVIDIA partners are effectively controlled by Chinese firms, with executives linked to Chinese military institutions and blacklisted entities. These entities leverage their U.S. registration to procure high-end AI chips and circumvent export controls by rerouting hardware to China via third-party jurisdictions.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 多项调查证实，部分位于加利福尼亚州的NVIDIA授权合作伙伴实际受中国资本控制，其高管背景关联中国军事院校及被列入贸易黑名单的实体。这些主体利用美国注册身份获取高端AI芯片，并通过东南亚等第三方渠道规避出口管制，向中国境内输送算力资源。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Investigations reveal that several California-based NVIDIA partners are effectively controlled by Chinese firms, with executives linked to Chinese military institutions and blacklisted entities. These entities leverage their U.S. registration to procure high-end AI chips and circumvent export controls by rerouting hardware to China via third-party jurisdictions.

fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】受中国资本控制的加州科技公司、NVIDIA在美国出口管制政策与商业供应链环境：规避出口限制获取高端AI芯片并进行非法跨境转售
【起因与机理】地缘政治竞争背景下，中国对高算力硬件的刚需与美国技术封锁政策的博弈
【关键数据与实测】The company's U.S. revenue fell from $201 million to $4.7 million this year.。
【各方立场与态度】现有出口管制政策在供应链穿透与终端监测方面存在显著漏洞。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] High demand for computing power in China vs. U.S. technology blockade
[Key Metrics] Nvidia had almost $20 billion in sales to China last year.
[Industry Impact & Outlook] Significant gaps identified in current export control enforcement and supply chain traceability.

title: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
title_en: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
author: Emma Roth
content_snippet:
Amazon is on the hook to recall more than 400,000 hazardous products after losing its legal battle against the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). The US District Court for the District of Maryland ruled in favor of the CPSC, which argued that Amazon is a distributor of goods, not a logistics provider, making it responsible for carrying out recalls of third-party products.

Amazon sued the CPSC in March 2025 after the agency ordered Amazon to recall over 400,000 “Fulfilled by Amazon” p
summary_en: The U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland ruled that Amazon acts as a distributor, not merely a logistics provider, regarding its 'Fulfilled by Amazon' services. Consequently, the company is mandated to comply with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's order to recall over 400,000 hazardous third-party products, including faulty carbon monoxide detectors and non-compliant children's apparel.

summary_en: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Deputy Steve Feinberg explored invoking the 1950 Defense Production Act to pressure Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. title: US chip-access curbs and anti-distillation measures are reportedly already slowing Chinese AI labs
title_en: US chip-access curbs and anti-distillation measures are reportedly already slowing Chinese AI labs
author: Matthias Bastian
content_snippet:
The US is tightening its grip in the AI race with China, and the push is already having an effect, according to The Information. Chinese AI developers including Deepseek, Moonshot AI, and Alibaba have been under pressure since September, squeezed by restrictions on Chinese firms' remote access to advanced Nvidia chips in foreign data centers and by successful anti-distillation measures from OpenAI and Anthropic.

As a result, many ongoing projects are facing delays, the report says. Last month,
summary_en: Restrictions on remote access to advanced chips and anti-distillation defenses from US-based model providers are widening the development gap between Chinese AI labs and US incumbents. Estimates from DeepSeek indicate a potential nine-month lag without distillation, forcing firms like Moonshot AI and Alibaba to pivot toward domestic silicon and intensified internal RL research.

author: Matthias Bastian
content_snippet:

AI must be governed by "legitimate democratic processes,"Amodei wrote. Political decisions should stay

author: Kai Nicol-Schwarz

Jack Duhamel

title: How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
title_en: How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
author: Casey Crownhart
content_snippet:
In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right.

Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity demand with other power sources, including renewables like wind and solar supported by batteries. But the reality in the US so far is that the data center boom is helping to fuel a massive natural-gas resurgence.

title: PrismML shrinks a 54 GB language model to 5.9 GB by reducing every weight to just three possible values

author: Jonathan Kemper
content_snippet:
Startup PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an updated version of its aggressively compressed language model. It's based on Qwen3.8-27B and takes up just 5.9 GB of memory, same as its predecessor. That's possible because of ternary quantization, where each weight can only be one of three values (−1, 0, or +1) instead of the usual 16-bit storage. At full precision, a model this size would need about 54 GB.

Bonsai 2.5 is designed to perform more reliably on agentic tasks that involve lon

Washington has spent years stopping advanced AI chips from physically reaching China. It turns out the chips never had to travel at all.

On Monday, the US Commerce Department issued a rule aimed at Chinese companies that tap high-end AI hardware sitting in data centers outside China. The move lands hardest on Southeast Asia, a region that has been building server farms at a brisk clip.

The rule comes from the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS. It is an interim final

title: MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable

author: Manuel Uth
content_snippet:
MIT researchers have developed a method that makes training AI climate models faster, cheaper, and more reliable. According to MIT News, these emulators now need only a fraction of the data typically required.

summary_en: Researchers from MIT, ETH Zurich, and Imperial College London have developed a method to train AI climate emulators using synthetic data characterized by extreme environmental fluctuations, such as sudden CO2 spikes. This approach allows models to achieve high precision and robustness with only a single simulation run, significantly reducing computational demand.

title: AI is straining America’s open records systems

author: Rachel Courtland
content_snippet:

summary_en: AI-powered automation is triggering a surge in public records requests across the U.S., forcing local agencies to handle significantly increased volume and scope.
